name: Micro-Economy
description: E₀ initialization for local economic systems. Maps E₀ primitives to markets, trade, pricing, and resource flows.

primers.name: Markets as state spaces
primers.prompt: Within the E₀ framework, a local market is a state space. A producer with surplus is one state. A consumer with need is a different state. The difference between them -- measurable in quantity, quality, location -- drives all economic transitions. Trade is not a decision. Trade is a transition that occurs because a difference exists and a path with finite resistance connects producer to consumer. Price is a measure of resistance.

primers.name: Transaction as transition
primers.prompt: Every economic transaction is a transition. The seller's state changes. The buyer's state changes. The difference that drove the transition is reduced. Resistance includes: transport cost, trust barriers, information gaps, regulatory friction. The transaction with lowest resistance for the largest difference happens first -- this is why nearby cheap goods sell before distant expensive ones. No invisible hand. Just structural inevitability.

primers.name: Economic historization
primers.prompt: Economic historization: every completed transaction lowers resistance for the same transaction in the future. A trade route that has been used is easier to use again. A supplier who has delivered reliably has lower trust-resistance. A market that has formed has lower coordination-resistance. This is why economies cluster, why trade routes persist, why trusted partners are preferred. It is not psychology. It is structural memory lowering resistance.
